writing.honesty: FIEZEL does not predict IELTS or TOEFL scores. This rubric is a tool for practice and feedback; official bands are only issued by official exams.

rubric.note: Five criteria, each scored 0-4. The first four follow the IELTS Writing criteria family; the fifth separates tone and neatness so they can be practiced independently.

task_response.label: Task achievement / response
task_response.asks: Are all parts of the prompt addressed, and is the position clear?
levels: Did not address the task, or wrote about a different topic.
Touches on the topic but misses most of the prompt's requirements; position is unreadable.
Addresses most requirements; the position is present but shifts or is underdeveloped.
Addresses all requirements with a clear position; some ideas still lack sufficient support.
Addresses all requirements with a clear and consistent position; each main idea is developed with relevant reasons or examples.

coherence_cohesion.label: Coherence and cohesion
coherence_cohesion.asks: Can the flow be followed without re-reading?
levels: No discernible flow.
Ideas jump around; almost no paragraphs or cohesive devices.
Paragraphs exist, but some ideas are misplaced or cohesive devices are repetitive.
Logical paragraphs with appropriate cohesive devices; occasional loose connections between sentences.
Each paragraph has one central idea, the sequence is logical, and references between sentences flow without repetitive markers.

lexical_resource.label: Lexical resource
lexical_resource.asks: Is the vocabulary sufficiently precise and varied for the topic?
levels: Vocabulary is too limited to convey the intended meaning.
Only basic words; heavy repetition and frequent word choice errors.
Sufficient for daily topics; less common words often miss the mark in meaning.
Varied and generally precise, including some topical vocabulary; occasional errors do not impede understanding.
Fluent and precise, including natural collocations and expressions; word choice errors are very rare.

grammatical_range_accuracy.label: Grammatical range and accuracy
grammatical_range_accuracy.asks: Are the sentence structures varied and correct?
levels: Structures are not yet formed as sentences.
Almost entirely short, repetitive sentences; errors hinder comprehension.
A mix of simple and compound sentences; errors are frequent but the meaning is still captured.
Diverse structures including complex clauses; most sentences are error-free.
Wide and controlled range of structures; errors are only occasional and do not distract.

register_mechanics.label: Register and mechanics
register_mechanics.asks: Is the tone appropriate for the reader, and is the punctuation neat?
levels: Tone and neatness cannot yet be assessed.
Tone is inappropriate for the task; many spelling and punctuation deviations.
Tone shifts between formal and casual; spelling or punctuation errors are quite visible.
Tone is appropriate for the task; few spelling and punctuation errors.
Tone is consistent and suitable for the reader; spelling, punctuation, and paragraphing are neat.

w-ja-a1-01.hint: Describe your day in five sentences using the particles は・を・に・で.
w-ja-a1-01.focus: particles は・を・に・で in daily sentences

w-ja-a1-02.hint: Who were you with yesterday, where were you, and what did you do? Use the particles と and で.
w-ja-a1-02.focus: Particle と (together with) and で (location of an activity)

w-ja-a1-03.hint: Describe the objects on the table using これ・それ・あれ.
w-ja-a1-03.focus: これ／それ／あれ based on distance from the speaker

w-ja-a1-04.hint: Write down the items you want at the store using この・その・あの.
w-ja-a1-04.focus: この／その／あの as noun modifiers

w-ja-a1-05.hint: Write your family's occupations and hometown using the particle の.
w-ja-a1-05.focus: の for possession, origin, and classification

w-ja-a1-06.hint: Write whose belongings are in your room, such as わたしの／ともだちの.
w-ja-a1-06.focus: Order of の: owner first, object follows

w-ja-a1-07.hint: Write about your favorite city using -i and -na adjectives.
w-ja-a1-07.focus: い vs な adjectives before nouns

w-ja-a1-08.hint: Write yesterday's weather, such as あつかったです／しずかでした.
w-ja-a1-08.focus: Past tense of い and な adjectives

w-ja-a1-09.hint: What is in your room? Use あります and います.
w-ja-a1-09.focus: あります for inanimate objects, います for living things

w-ja-a1-10.hint: Where is the cat? Use うえ・した・なか.

w-ja-a1-11.hint: Write five things you do every day in the ます form.
w-ja-a1-11.focus: ます stem of godan, ichidan, and irregular verbs

w-ja-a1-12.hint: Make four short sentences using たべる・のむ・いく・する.
w-ja-a1-12.focus: Verb groups and their polite forms

w-ja-a1-13.hint: Write your plans for tomorrow using ます and ません.
w-ja-a1-13.focus: ます／ません for plans and refusals

w-ja-a1-14.hint: Write what you did and did not do last week.
w-ja-a1-14.focus: ました／ませんでした for the past tense

w-ja-a1-15.hint: Write three things you did not do yesterday.
w-ja-a1-15.focus: Past negative form ませんでした

w-ja-a1-16.hint: Write foods you did not like when you were a child.
w-ja-a1-16.focus: Past negative for nouns and な adjectives

w-ja-a1-17.hint: Write five questions for a new friend.
w-ja-a1-17.focus: なに・だれ・どこ・いつ + か at the end of a sentence

w-ja-a1-18.hint: Write questions for a store clerk using いくら・どこ・なに.
w-ja-a1-18.focus: Interrogative words for price, place, and thing

w-ja-a1-19.hint: Write the contents of your bag along with their quantities.

w-ja-a1-20.hint: Write the number of family members you have and their ages.
w-ja-a1-20.focus: Counter にん (including ひとり／ふたり) and さい

w-ja-a1-21.hint: Write your one-week schedule, including days and times.
w-ja-a1-21.focus: ようび, month/date markers, and に for specific times

w-ja-a1-22.hint: What time do you wake up and go to sleep? Write with the times.
w-ja-a1-22.focus: じ／ふん and the particle に for hours

w-ja-a1-23.hint: Write your morning activities, connected with the ~て form.
w-ja-a1-23.focus: formation of the て form by verb group

w-ja-a1-24.hint: Write what you are doing right now using ~ています.
w-ja-a1-24.focus: ています for ongoing actions

w-ja-a2-01.hint: Write today's diary entry entirely in the plain form (not です・ます).
w-ja-a2-01.focus: plain form as a written diary style

w-ja-a2-02.hint: Write a message to a friend using both positive AND negative plain forms.
w-ja-a2-02.focus: positive and negative plain forms in casual messages

w-ja-a2-03.hint: Write from waking up in the morning until leaving the house, using 〜てから and 〜ています.
w-ja-a2-03.focus: sequence with てから and ongoing states with ています

w-ja-a2-04.hint: Write what you prepare before going out, using 〜ておきます three times.

w-ja-a2-05.hint: Write what you can and cannot do yet in Japanese, using the potential form.

w-ja-a2-06.hint: Introduce various things that can be done in your town. Also use 〜ことができます.
w-ja-a2-06.focus: two ways to express ability: kanoukei and ことができる

w-ja-a2-07.hint: Write your plans for this year using 〜ようと思っています and 〜つもりです.
w-ja-a2-07.focus: intention: ようと思っている vs つもり

w-ja-a2-08.hint: Write a message inviting a friend, distinguishing between the use of 〜ましょう and 〜ませんか.
w-ja-a2-08.focus: invitation: ましょう which assumes agreement vs ませんか which offers an option

w-ja-a2-09.hint: Write what your parents made you do when you were a child, using the causative-passive.
w-ja-a2-09.focus: causative-passive させられる for unwanted things

w-ja-a2-10.hint: Introduce a famous building in your town using the passive (no need to mention the creator).

w-ja-a2-11.hint: What would you do if you had money? Use 〜たら and 〜ても together.
w-ja-a2-11.focus: condition たら vs concession ても

w-ja-a2-12.hint: Write advice for a friend visiting Japan for the first time. Use 〜なら twice.
w-ja-a2-12.focus: なら picking up a condition from the interlocutor

w-ja-a2-13.hint: Write about something broken at home, distinguishing between intransitive and transitive verbs.
w-ja-a2-13.focus: transitive-intransitive pairs and who performs the action

w-ja-a2-14.hint: Write the steps for tidying up a room. Use 〜てあります or 〜ています.
w-ja-a2-14.focus: state of results: てある (prepared) vs ている (ongoing)

w-ja-a2-15.hint: Write about an experience of being helped by someone, using 〜てもらいました and 〜てくれました.
w-ja-a2-15.focus: direction of a favor: もらう (I am the subject) vs くれる (they are the subject)

w-ja-a2-16.hint: Write about gifts you gave and received. Explain to whom and from whom.
w-ja-a2-16.focus: あげる・くれる・もらう and their marker particles

w-ja-a2-17.hint: Introduce news you read and then write your opinion, using 〜と思います.
w-ja-a2-17.focus: quoting content with と and expressing opinions

w-ja-a2-18.hint: Write what your parents told you to do, using 〜ように言われました.
w-ja-a2-18.focus: reporting instructions/commands with ように言う

w-ja-a2-19.hint: Write about your favorite place, using three modifying clauses such as 〜があるところ.
w-ja-a2-19.focus: noun-modifying relative clauses in plain form

w-ja-a2-20.hint: Introduce the person you met yesterday, using the pattern わたしがきのう会った人.
w-ja-a2-20.focus: が inside relative clauses instead of は

w-ja-a2-21.hint: City or countryside, which is more comfortable? Use 〜より, 〜のほうが, and いちばん.
w-ja-a2-21.focus: comparison of two things and superlatives

w-ja-a2-22.hint: Compare this year with last year, using 〜にくらべて.
w-ja-a2-22.focus: にくらべて for introducing a point of comparison

w-ja-a2-23.hint: Explain your school rules, using 〜なければなりません and 〜てはいけません.

w-ja-a2-24.hint: Write what you do not need to do during the holidays, using 〜なくてもいいです.
w-ja-a2-24.focus: なくてもいい: exemption from duty, not prohibition

w-ja-a2-25.hint: Write your reasons for studying Japanese, using 〜ので or 〜から.
w-ja-a2-25.focus: reasons with ので (polite) and から (direct)

w-ja-a2-26.hint: Write about something that did not go well, using 〜のに.
w-ja-a2-26.focus: のに: reality running counter to expectations

w-ja-a2-27.hint: Write about your most interesting experience so far, using 〜たことがあります.
w-ja-a2-27.focus: past experiences with たことがある

w-ja-a2-28.hint: Write about your weekly activities, using よく, ときどき, and めったに〜ません.
w-ja-a2-28.focus: frequency adverbs and their required polarity

w-ja-a2-29.hint: Write an email to your teacher, distinguishing between humble and honorific forms.
w-ja-a2-29.focus: keigo: humble forms for one's own actions, honorific forms for the teacher's actions

w-ja-a2-30.hint: Write a store announcement, using お〜ください and 〜ございます.
w-ja-a2-30.focus: honorific request structures and ございます for items

w-ja-b1-01.hint: Write 4–5 sentences about new habits you have recently started and study plans you wish to continue (use patterns: 〜はじめる, 〜つづける, 〜ていく).

w-ja-b1-02.hint: Write about how your city has changed over the past few years and how you think it will change in the future (use patterns: 〜てくる, 〜ていく, 〜おわる).

w-ja-b1-03.hint: Write 4–5 sentences about this weekend's weather forecast and your impression upon seeing the sky condition (use patterns: 〜そうだ [hearsay], 〜そうだ [appearance], 〜らしい).

w-ja-b1-04.hint: Explain news about a restaurant or recommended movie you heard from a friend along with your impression (use patterns: 〜らしい, 〜みたいだ, 〜そうだ).

w-ja-b1-05.hint: Write about a childhood experience when you were told by your parents or a teacher to do something you didn't like at first and how you feel now (use the causative-passive form 〜せられる／〜させられる).

w-ja-b1-06.hint: Write 4–5 sentences about an incident when you were asked to wait or help a senior at a club activity or part-time job (use patterns: 〜される, 〜させられる).

w-ja-b1-07.hint: Write about a goal you still want to fight for even though you know it is difficult, along with your reasons (use patterns: 〜ても, 〜のに, 〜にもかかわらず).

w-ja-b1-08.hint: Write 4–5 sentences about an experience when the actual result differed from your initial expectation (use patterns: 〜のに, 〜くせに, 〜わりには).

w-ja-b1-09.hint: Write a short announcement of 4–5 sentences for school library users or local public facility patrons (use patterns: 〜について, 〜によって, 〜に関して).

w-ja-b1-10.hint: Write about how our lives and shopping habits have changed thanks to the spread of the internet (use patterns: 〜によって, 〜に対して, 〜を中心に).

w-ja-b1-11.hint: Write a casual message to a close friend recounting an incident when you accidentally forgot or made a small mistake (use spoken forms: 〜ちゃう／〜じゃう, 〜とく, 〜なきゃ).

w-ja-b1-12.hint: Write a short chat of 4–5 sentences with a friend to discuss things that must be prepared before leaving for a trip (use spoken forms: 〜とく, 〜なきゃ, 〜てる).

w-ja-b1-13.hint: Write about the experience of pursuing a hobby or sport where the more you practice, the more proficient you become (use patterns: 〜ば〜ほど, 〜ほど, 〜くらい).

w-ja-b1-14.hint: Write about the most enjoyable or surprising experience you have ever had and describe how great the impression was (use patterns: 〜ほど, 〜くらい, 〜ば〜ほど).

w-ja-b1-15.hint: Write about an item you decided to buy after hesitating, as well as things you learned while searching for information about it (use patterns: 〜うちに, 〜うえで, 〜ついでに).

w-ja-b1-16.hint: Write 4–5 sentences about errands you want to finish at the same time when going out on a day off and activities you want to do while it is still daylight (use patterns: 〜ついでに, 〜うちに, 〜最中に).

w-ja-b2-01.hint: Elaborate in 5–6 sentences on the benefits of learning new technology, not only in terms of work but also daily life (use patterns: 〜だけでなく, 〜に限らず, 〜ばかりか).

w-ja-b2-02.hint: Explain the reason why local cultural events are popular across various generations, not limited to young people alone (use patterns: 〜に限らず, 〜のみならず, 〜うえに).

w-ja-b2-03.hint: Write in 5–6 sentences about environmental or health habits that we inevitably must review immediately (use patterns: 〜ざるを得ない, 〜ないわけにはいかない, 〜しかない).

w-ja-b2-04.hint: Present the reasons why responsibilities or promises we have agreed to must be fulfilled until the end (use patterns: 〜以上は, 〜からには, 〜ないわけにはいかない).

w-ja-b2-05.hint: Write about things you want to do immediately once preparations are complete in welcoming a project or new life (use patterns: 〜にあたって, 〜次第, 〜に際して).

w-ja-b2-06.hint: Write 5–6 sentences about what you directly felt right when a major exam or presentation ended, along with subsequent events (use patterns: 〜とたんに, 〜かと思うと, 〜次第).

w-ja-b2-07.hint: Present the advantages and challenges of urban redevelopment when viewed from the perspective of local residents (use patterns: 〜から見れば, 〜という点では, 〜にこたえて).

w-ja-b2-08.hint: Write about the importance of shopping from the perspective of whether an item can be used durably in the long term, rather than just its price (use patterns: 〜という点では, 〜からすると, 〜をもとに).

w-ja-b2-09.hint: Write about a past experience that makes you regret not consulting earlier, as well as the lesson you learned (use patterns: 〜ばかりに, 〜あげく, 〜ことだ).

w-ja-b2-10.hint: Write 5–6 sentences about the decision you made after long consideration and the first step that must be taken to achieve your goal (use patterns: 〜末に, 〜ないことには, 〜ことだ).

w-ja-b2-11.hint: Write a polite business email to a business partner to express gratitude for sending documents while also conveying next week's visit plan (use patterns: 拝見する, 伺う, 申し上げます).

w-ja-b2-12.hint: Write a 5–6 sentence seminar invitation email explaining the event schedule and requesting a reply confirmation by Friday at the latest (use patterns: ご〜させていただきます, 承る, 〜ていただきたいと存じます).

w-ja-c1-01.hint: Write a formal 5–6 sentence argument about a situation when the government inevitably has to take firm action for public safety (use patterns: 〜ざるを得ない, 〜ずにはおかない, 〜ないではすまない).

w-ja-c1-02.hint: Write about the power of literary works or historical records that invariably stir the conscience of anyone who witnesses them (use patterns: 〜ずにはおかない, 〜べくもない, 〜にやまれぬ).

w-ja-c1-03.hint: Write a 5–6 sentence opinion on equality before the law, that even if someone is a ruler or a well-known expert, no exceptions are justified (use patterns: 〜といえども, 〜であれ, 〜にせよ).

w-ja-c1-04.hint: Write about the meaning of giving firm reprimands to juniors precisely because we genuinely think about their future (use patterns: 〜ばこそ, 〜とて, 〜からといって).

w-ja-c1-05.hint: Depict in 5–6 sentences how society and the market react immediately as soon as major news or new technology is announced (use patterns: 〜や否や, 〜が早いか, 〜なり).

w-ja-c1-06.hint: Write your study strategy for overcoming the problem of memorizing vocabulary or new knowledge that is immediately forgotten as soon as memorization is finished (use patterns: 〜そばから, 〜が早いか, 〜や否や).

w-ja-c1-07.hint: Express your opinion in 5–6 sentences that as a leader or a doctor, one is obligated to uphold high ethics at all times (use patterns: 〜たるもの, 〜ならではの, 〜に恥じない).

w-ja-c1-08.hint: Explain why traditional craft works or years of research results deserve international praise and trust (use patterns: 〜に足る, 〜に値する, 〜ならではの).

w-ja-c1-09.hint: Write a 5–6 sentence analysis with the theme that the success or failure of organizational reform or negotiation depends entirely on future handling steps (use patterns: 〜いかんだ, 〜いかんによっては, 〜にかかっている).

w-ja-c1-10.hint: Write about a competency-based evaluation system regardless of background, as well as an indomitable attitude that does not flinch in facing obstacles (use patterns: 〜のいかんによらず, 〜をものともせず, 〜に至っては).

w-ja-c2-01.hint: Write an academic essay paragraph with the thesis that the rise of AI does not stop at technical innovation alone, but is none other than a structural transformation of human society (use patterns: 〜にとどまらず, 〜にほかならない, 〜のみならず).

w-ja-c2-02.hint: Write a critical review of about 6 sentences that the collapse of organizations ignoring internal oversight is a logical inevitability that is bound to happen (use patterns: 〜べくして, 〜といっても過言ではない, 〜にほかならない).

w-ja-c2-03.hint: Write an editorial text arguing that covering up facts to maintain personal power is an action completely inappropriate for public officials (use the patterns: 〜んがために, 〜にあるまじき, 〜べからず).

w-ja-c2-04.hint: Write a high-literary-style essay about the unbearable regret over the destruction of cultural heritage and how easy it is to understand the pain of the victims (use the patterns: 〜に難くない, 〜を禁じ得ない, 〜に堪えない).

w-ja-c2-05.hint: Discuss the relationship between planning quality and actual execution from the perspective that no matter how brilliant a policy is, if it is not carried out, everything ends up in vain (use the patterns: 〜もさることながら, 〜ばそれまでだ, 〜といったらない).

w-ja-c2-06.hint: Write about a principled negotiation stance: rather than compromising to the point of sacrificing principles, it is far better to withdraw, but if the opposing party makes concessions, renegotiation is not entirely out of the question (use the patterns: 〜くらいなら…ほうがましだ, 〜ないものでもない, 〜とばかりに).

w-ja-c2-07.hint: Write an executive-level official letter to partner board members congratulating them on the company's prosperity, thanking them for their exceptional support thus far, and requesting that they review the attached contract draft (use the patterns: ご清栄, ご高配を賜り, ご査収のほど).

w-ja-c2-08.hint: Write an executive-level official letter of apology acknowledging that the error that occurred was solely due to one's own personal shortcomings, asking for understanding, and promising a detailed explanation upon meeting in person (use the patterns: 不徳の致すところ, ご容赦くださいますよう, 拝眉の上).
